Subject: High p99 + 502s on our on-prem cluster (urgent)

Rafael —

We started seeing intermittent 502/504s and very high tail latency (p99 > 6s) on our private deployment in our DC-chi cluster starting ~06:50 PDT this morning. Impacting both interactive chat and nightly inference jobs; throughput for some routes has dropped ~30% compared to yesterday. Our ops team collected traces and pushed aggregated logs to S3; attaching a small sample here.

Short timeline:
- 06:50: first user reports of slow responses
- 07:10: retries + 502s spike (~2% of requests)
- 07:20–08:00: oscillating p95/p99, some sessions failing mid-run

We haven't deployed any model changes on our side in the last 24h. Can Redwood take a look? We need this prioritized — this affects several clinician workflows.

Attachments: cluster-logs-20260903.tar.gz (log summary), client-traces-20260903.json (sample traces)

Rafael / team / Priya — quick triage notes after a cursory look at the attached traces and the head-of-logs: 

Observations (from traces + node metrics):
- Large batch spikes correlate with sustained NVMe IO latency spikes on 2 nodes (nvme0n1). Disk IO waits coincide with increased decode durations leading to KV cache churn.
- KV cache size for the model variant servicing the clinician route grew by ~38% over the last 6 hours (likely long token sequences from a small subset of clients). That growth triggers more frequent cache evictions and backend rehydration which amplifies p99 latency.
- We saw a small burst of TLS socket resets (RST) between 07:05–07:18 on the same nodes; connections recovered but a few inflight requests returned 502.
- No model binary changes on customer side; looks infra/resource & batching/caching behavior.

Immediate mitigation recommendations (low risk):
1) Set a temporary small-batch fallback policy on the clinician route: max_batch_tokens=1536, max_batch_size=6; this reduces tail latency while allowing throughput to stay reasonable.
2) Enable KV cache soft-limit to 6GB for that model variant and turn on eviction logging to validate behavior.
3) Throttle long-context requests at the ingress for a short window (requests > 8k tokens -> reject with 429 + friendly message) — ask customer to opt-in to this.

If mitigation works, follow-up actions:
- Patch runtime to improve background rehydration prioritization (we have a patch that sequences rehydration with lower IO concurrency) — requires a short maintenance window and a restart of the serving pool on the two affected nodes.
- Investigate NVMe health and evening GC windows on BlueHaven host config with their infra team.

I'll prepare a short playbook and a deploy plan. If customer approves the fallback and throttles, we can reduce p99 within 15–30 minutes.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: High p99 + 502s on our on-prem cluster (urgent)

Hi Priya — thanks for the flag and for the logs. Laura's recommendations make sense and are low-risk for an immediate relief path. Proposed next steps: 

1) Immediate: we will apply the small-batch fallback and KV cache soft-limit remotely. This is a config-only change and does not require node restarts. We will monitor live metrics for 30 minutes post-change.
2) Containment: we will enable an ingress throttle for requests > 8000 tokens — this is reversible and we will notify affected clients at your direction.
3) If metrics don't normalize: schedule a 30-minute maintenance window tonight (09/03 22:00–22:30 PDT) to roll a runtime patch to reduce rehydration IO concurrency on the two impacted nodes. The patch requires restarting the serving manager on each node; we will do a rolling restart with a canary first.

We can also offer a small service credit for any measurable SLA miss during the incident window — Rafael will coordinate commercial.

Please reply with a quick thumbs-up if you authorize the config changes now. We will attach a detailed playbook: proposed-mitigation-playbook-20260903.pdf and post-run logs.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
